role: SessionRecoveryCoordinator extension for recovering sessions from the app's own on-disk/iCloud backups, the trash, the H10's internal recording (workout/overnight augment, interrupted-workout auto-recovery), paused-state restore, and the one-time merge-data-loss repair migration; plus file-scope helpers and the InterruptedWorkoutAutoRecovery in-flight registry.
types: SessionRecoveryCoordinator: extension — backup/trash/strap recovery and merge repair
SessionRecoveryCoordinator.WatchRouteRecoveryResult: enum — recovered/distanceOnly/noRoute/failed outcome of Apple Health route recovery
SessionRecoveryCoordinator.StrapAugmentResult: enum — merged/notConnected/noStrapData/failed for workout strap merge
SessionRecoveryCoordinator.MergeDamage: struct — which merge-repair conditions a linked child session has
InterruptedWorkoutAutoRecovery: enum — lock-protected static set of session ids currently being auto-recovered at launch
SessionRecoveryCoordinator.MergeRepairOutcome: struct — repaired / failed counts of one merge-repair run
SessionRecoveryCoordinator.LinkedRepairResult: enum — repaired / unchanged / failed for one linked night
AutoRecoveryAttempts: enum (file-private, @MainActor) — the launch auto-recovery attempt counter, one UserDefaults dictionary holding only the workout being recovered
state: ud:reviewedRecoveredWorkoutIds (static let reviewedRecoveredKey, string array capped at 50)

ud:autoRecoverAttempts (AutoRecoveryAttempts.key: [uuidString: Int] holding only the workout being auto-recovered; replaced on each counted attempt, removed on its successful recovery). Per-session 'autoRecoverAttempts_<uuid>' keys written by earlier versions are no longer read or removed
toplevel: Declares the three result enums, MergeDamage, MergeRepairOutcome and LinkedRepairResult inside the extension; file-scope private helpers unrecoveredBackupIds/newestWorkoutBackup; the file-private AutoRecoveryAttempts enum (UserDefaults key 'autoRecoverAttempts', limit 3); InterruptedWorkoutAutoRecovery enum with a static lock initialised to an empty set.

Restores a trashed session: un-marks it deleted (and tells iCloud trashRestore); if the archive still holds the id as deleted (the un-mark failed, which the service only logs) it logs the cause, abandons the iCloud restore and returns nil without rebuilding (the archive would refuse the write). Otherwise puts back the trashed file if the trash kept it, else rebuilds from the raw backup; on rebuild failure abandons the iCloud restore.

branches.cond: id still in archive.deletedIds after the un-mark

branches.effect: restoreFromTrashFailed abandons the iCloud restore (the un-mark is not rolled back); returns nil

units.does: Puts a trashed session's kept file back: loads it from the trash, links/supersedes any same-night session recorded since, archives it with skipSameNightMerge, discards the trash copy, marks its raw backup archived, force-reuploads to iCloud and bumps the archive signal.

branches.effect: continues; nil → returns nil (caller falls back to raw-backup rebuild)
logs error and returns nil (trash copy kept); caller then tries raw-backup rebuild

units.does: Pass-through to SessionRecoveryService.permanentlyDelete: drop trash copy, raw backup, iCloud live backup and the deleted-id record.
Pass-through to SessionRecoveryService.deleteLostSessions: marks each id deleted in the archive (errors logged).

branches.effect: continues; otherwise returns nil (disk backup only)

branches.effect: returns points on the workout clock; otherwise logs and returns nil

units.does: Review/trim card Save: clips the archived workout's RR series at endSec and re-finalizes it through WorkoutRecoveryService (discarding backups). With <30 beats left it keeps the workout untrimmed and closes the review (marked reviewed). When the re-finalize fails it logs an error and leaves the card up and the session unreviewed, so the trim can be saved again; on success it bumps the archive signal and closes the review.

branches.cond: archived session or its rrSeries missing
branches.effect: `?? []` → clipped empty → <30 → closes the review, nothing changed

units.does: Marks the recovered workout reviewed (so its card does not come back) and clears the review card.

Review card Discard: deletes the archived recovered workout (failure logged via attempt). Only when the delete landed does it bump the archive signal and close the review; a failed delete leaves the card up and the session unreviewed so Discard can be retried. The raw backup is kept either way.

Recovers a crash-shortened workout's route/distance from Apple Health: first a Watch workout GPS route (>=2 points) re-finalized through WorkoutRecoveryService; else HealthKit passive walking/running distance if it beats the recorded distance by >50 m (.noRoute when it does not, .failed when the rewrite itself fails).

branches.cond: HealthKit route exists with >=2 locations AND recoverWorkout with that track succeeds
branches.effect: notifies and returns .recovered; otherwise falls to passive distance

units.does: Calls WorkoutRecoveryService.recover with the given RR points and either an override GPS track (discarding backups) or an override distance.

'Recover session' for an archived workout: with the strap connected, downloads its recording of this session, merges it with the archived RR (SessionRecoveryMath.mergedWorkoutPoints), re-finalizes with auto-trim and returns duration/beat count.

branches.effect: beat count falls back to merged.count

units.does: 'Pull from strap & re-merge' for an overnight scored from the stream: unless already device/composite-sourced, reconnects, downloads the strap's recording of this night, merges via DataSourceSelector (device preferred), persists the merged series + provenance, then re-scores through reanalyzeSession.

branches.effect: returns .noStrapData (also when refused because the strap's recording is considered live, see pullStrapRecording)
existing = [] and strap points alone go to the selector

returns strapRR; otherwise nil (no merge reported)

units.does: Re-scores the merged overnight via collector.reanalyzeSession (which reloads from disk and re-archives), bumps the archive signal and returns .merged with source and beat count; the score is the rescored session's, or nil when the reanalysis failed (the archived score predates the merge).

branches.effect: uses the persisted-but-unrescored session for source and beats; score reported nil

units.does: Begins a strap transfer (BLE hold) and reconnects for it; returns whether the reconnect succeeded.

Downloads the strap recording that belongs to an archived session (started during it), placed on the session's clock; refuses while a live session owns the strap; a downloaded recording dated outside the session (or undated) is handed to the rescue backup instead.

branches.effect: proceeds to download; otherwise logs and returns []

branches.effect: returns its points on the session clock; otherwise (nil start or later start) rescues it via onUnrecoveredDataRescued and returns []

units.does: Resolves the interrupted workout to recover: the persisted crash flag when it names a non-live, un-archived workout (flaggedInterruptedWorkoutId); else (off-main) the newest un-archived, un-deleted workout backup indexed and captured in the last 24 h that is not live.

branches.effect: returns it; otherwise scans backups in a detached task

branches.cond: no marker, not a workout, live, or already archived

units.does: Clears the persisted recording state only when it names the given session id.

Launch auto-recovery of a crashed workout. Before any await it registers the workout the persisted marker names as running (InterruptedWorkoutAutoRecovery), so the launch alert's Save waits on it; then finds the interrupted workout (marker or newest backup) and registers that too. If the attempt budget (3) remains and the strap is reached, still records and no other recording has started, it counts the attempt, rebuilds via recoverWorkoutFromBackup and on success clears the marker and the attempt count. Both registrations end when it returns.

branches.cond: the marker names a non-live, un-archived workout
branches.effect: registers it as running before the scan
returns (registration of the flagged id ends)

branches.cond: attempt budget exhausted, or strap not reached / not recording / a new recording started
branches.effect: returns without counting an attempt; marker left for the manual card
returns leaving marker and count; otherwise clears both

units.does: Whether launch auto-recovery may pull the strap: the strap is reconnected and still records (strapReadyForAutoRecovery), and the persisted marker does not now name a different session (a workout started while the strap was being reached). Logs and returns false otherwise.

branches.cond: strap not reachable or not recording

units.does: Begins a transfer, reconnects, refreshes the strap's recording status within the feature-ready window and returns whether it is still recording on device.

Launch recovery of an interrupted overnight into a resumable paused state: SessionRecoveryService rebuilds/analyses from backup and archives it paused; then the collector enters paused state, takes the night's capture choice from the recording marker (so Resume arms the strap as the night did), persists the paused-session marker (with that choice) and clears the recording marker.

branches.cond: service returned nil (no backup or archive failed)

Pure: rebuilds a child night's beats appended to the parent's, shifted by max(parent duration, wall-clock gap between starts); for v5-corrupted children only the tail after parentBeatCount is taken.

branches.cond: parent last point endMs/t_ms nil (empty parent)

units.does: One-time migration body: walks every linked overnight session, repairing each whose merge was lost; counts repaired nights and nights whose repair could not be written; bumps the archive signal if any was repaired; returns both counts. Not cancellable (its only caller keeps no task handle).
